best_echo_sets.commentary: Offers a 10% unconditional Energy Regen% boost taking some pressure off your gear when aiming at ER breakpoints. Also upon using Outro, grants the next character switching in a 22.5% ATK boost, amplifying any of your main damage dealers burst windows.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Supportive Echo that can be run at the cost of a sizeable chunk of damage for the character who equips, trading personal gain for team benefits. Should always be used and immediately switch cancelled right before performing an Outro, leading to another DPS. When done so will grant the next character switching in 12% increased DMG% which when combined with the 5P Moonlit set which also grants 22.5% ATK% under the same conditions makes for a sizeable boost. While the echo does lower the damage of whoever wears it, it grants a massive chunk of energy on use usually saving 1 or sometimes even 2 Energy Regen sub stats that may otherwise be needed by the wearer allowing for some damage to be recovered.

best_echo_sets.commentary: Offers a 10% unconditional Healing% boost and an most importantly a 15% ATK% boost for the entire team, lasting 30 seconds whenever you heal yourself or any of your allies. This bonus can be triggered by character abilities and weapon effects, is easy to keep active 100% of the time and is a big help for all party members.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Simple summon Echo that can be cast any time (ideally right before the wielder's Outro), granting 10% ATK to the team for 20s (sufficient for 2 other teammates' rotation times if cast right before Outro) as well as 10% Energy Regen to the wielder to help with Energy requirements.

best_echo_sets.commentary: Offers a 10% unconditional Spectro DMG% boost, a 20% CRIT RATE buff for 15 seconds after inflicting Spectro Frazzle and further 15% Spectro DMG% boost for 15 seconds after attacking an enemy that has 10 Spectro Frazzle stacks. For characters that have the capability to inflict Spectro Frazzle in their kit the 20% CRIT RATE is all but permanant, while the 15% Spectro DMG boost should maintain decent uptime in Spectro Frazzle focused teams.

main_echo_options.echo_commentary: Offers an unconditional 12% Spectro DMG boost when active in a resonators Main Echo Slot and gains a 100% DMG bonus to attack against enemies inflicted by Spectro Frazzle. This echo is the go to choice for most resonators capable of inflicting Spectro Frazzle, who are focusing on damage and are looking to use the 5P Eternal Radiance set bonus.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Changli's signature weapon that's not only fantastic for her but also usable on all damage-focused Sword users who have a large portion of their damage originating from Resonance Skill damage. Offers a huge main stat of CRIT DMG% granting excellent scaling, 12% permanent ATK% and up to 56% increased Resonance Skill DMG% which should be at or close to full power during the bulk of your rotation when opening with one or two resonance skills.

Additionally has a good amount of Energy Regen, which on most characters will allow one sub-stat of Energy Regen to be allocated elsewhere to increase damage even further. Best Sword choice across the board with only S5 4â Swords having a chance to compete with it.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Powerful sword for Resonators spending minimal time on the field - the shorter the better. Best for Hybrid characters executing their rotation fast and infrequently, but less powerful on Main DPS characters that aim to spend extended time on field.

This effect can be triggered 1 time(s) every 12s. Oath reduces by 1 stack(s) every 2s. Equipped Resonator gains an additional 6 stack(s) of Oath upon defeating an enemy.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Often inferior to Commando of Conviction for DPS, this sword is still a great F2P 4* option for characters who need the energy boost. Realistically however, only consider this option over Commando of Conviction if you have energy problems on your character.

best_weapons.commentary_details: Exceptional all-around generic Sword gaining its bonus close to unconditionally as most Resonators almost always aim to make use of their Intro skill and very few characters spend more than 15 seconds on field during their duration.

For characters that use their Skill multiple times per rotation, this downside is a non-issue but for Main DPS characters who take up a lot of field time and don't use their skill often this sword can lose value.

Only use this team if you have a lot of quickswap experience, else consider other teams.
Make sure Spectro Rover is wielding the Moonlit Clouds set here.

Only best use case is in Quickswap with Zani and Phoebe, their rotation is super awkward and they're overall not worth using if you don't Quickswap;

sections.heading: Summary
paragraphs: Spectro Rover is a 5-star Spectro Sword character who is the only free-to-play Spectro Frazzle applier. Their kit focuses on applying Spectro Frazzle for their allies to take advantage of, and they act mostly as a sort of 3rd slot Support, but they're particular as they have almost no inherent kit buffs and effectively no Outro Skill.

sections.heading: Key Mechanics & Rotation Concepts
paragraphs: Spectro Rover is an especially dated 1.0 character that has a more unique design philosophy, the same way a lot of characters from the game's release do. A lot of characters had no identity on release, and Spectro Rover was one of those. However, in 2.0, they gained the following abilities that define their meta use case:
Their Ultimate applies 6 stacks of Spectro Frazzle to enemies hit;

Their Forte Skill applies 2 stacks of Spectro Frazzle and Shimmer to enemies hit, which prevents Spectro Frazzle counts from decreasing for 9s (they still deal their normal damage, but the stacks don't deplete upon dealing that damage as they normally would).

In total, to complete their rotation, they'll at least need to cast that Ultimate and 2 Forte Skills, which is a minimum of 10 Spectro Frazzle stacks applied per rotation. They may, however, do more than this in Quickswap.

Indeed, Spectro Rover has no inherent kit buffs that expire on Swap. Most characters in Spectro Rover's intended role have an Outro Skill that provides an amount of DMG Amplification to the next character, and it expires on swap. This is not their case, as their Outro just generates a field around themselves that slow enemies down to a crawl. Practically speaking, aside from adding some rotation consistency against more aggressive enemies, this is quite useless.

Most of their actual buffs are found in their Sequence nodes: free CRIT Rate, Energy Regen, Spectro & Liberation DMG Bonus. This only affects their own damage though. What's most relevant is their S4 and S6. Their S4 allows them to heal the entire party after casting Ultimate, and the S6 provides 10% Spectro RES Shred to all enemies hit by their Skill/Forte Skill. The healing is particularly important as it allows them to trigger the Rejuvenating Glow set for free, allowing them to act as a Spectro Frazzle-applying/RES shredding Support.

Finally, for their rotation, the only relevant combo to charge up some Forte is their Basic 2-3/Heavy Attack into Resonance & Aftertune. Those are special Heavy/Basic Attacks activated sequentially, Aftertune itself grants almost half of a Forte gauge. Half is what needs to be spent in order to cast a Forte Skill, and you get there with the Forte generated by a Basic 2-3 or a Heavy Attack.

These Forte Skills can also be followed up with a special Basic Attack called Resonating Echoes. In some rotations, this allows you to get enough Concerto quite quickly to trigger another character's Intro if they need it, even if Spectro Rover's own Outro is practically useless. And that's really all there is to say about their rotation.

sections.heading: Meta Position & Conclusion
paragraphs: Compared to say, a Verina or a Shorekeeper, in a Spectro Frazzle team, Spectro Rover has some clear advantages. Spectro RES shred and Spectro Frazzle application are both great additional resources that our 2 available Spectro Frazzle DPS, Zani and Phoebe make great use of.

However, Spectro Rover's damage buffing profile is very low, and their main utility is personal damage, Quickswap-friendliness and most important of all, Spectro Frazzle application. Through it, DPS Phoebe is enabled as Spectro Rover's Spectro Frazzle application is a necessity for her to do meaningful damage with her Starflash heavies.

Meanwhile, Zani's Spectro Frazzle application is already covered by Phoebe herself in Confession mode. Where Spectro Rover comes in is to provide even more fuel to Zani's Ultimate, as they're able to restore her Blaze bar mid-rotation through Quickswap in order to get her to do 1 or even 2 more Nightfalls depending on your rotation. This is highly significant for more advanced Zani rotations, and the Zani/Phoebe/Spectro Rover team played in Quickswap is the only reason why Zani is still meta relevant in the right hands today.

However, outside of these use cases, let's be honest - neither Phoebe nor Zani are meta-relevant units to begin with as things stand. If that wasn't enough, DPS Phoebe cannot be optimized enough to really keep up with the rest of the meta. Besides, Spectro Rover's own rotation is so slow and clunky outside of Quickswap that it's not even worth finishing all the way, at which point general Supports like Shorekeeper and Verina are simply better ideas.

In conclusion, Spectro Rover is a practically Quickswap-only unit for very specific teams that have long since dwindled in meta relevancy for most players. That is, Spectro Frazzle. Alongside both Zani and Phoebe in Quickswap rotations, Spectro Rover can prove quite strong as Zani's additional source of Blaze generation to execute more of her most powerful attacks. Outside of that use case, it's safe to say Spectro Rover is not a recommended investment in the current meta.

synergies.commentary: Absolution Phoebe needs a Spectro Frazzle applier to function, Spectro Rover being one of the main options to consider. This is because Spectro Rover's S6 Spectro RES Shred contributes to higher damage, and as their Ultimate has healing included, they can comfortably run both Rejuvenating Glow and Moonlit Clouds Echoes to adjust to Phoebe's teams, allowing for various teammate choices. Other than that, they work fantastically as a Support to the Phoebe-Zani team for Confession Phoebe as well.

Spectro Rover is an amazing pairing to Zani as a Support alongside Phoebe due to their Spectro RES Shred, Spectro Frazzle application, good personal damage and ability to trigger the Rejuvenating Glow set effect with their Ultimate. They can also act as a replacement for Phoebe if you don't own her, however they're problematic for a few reasons. While they do provide 10% Spectro RES Shred via their S6, their skill cooldowns are an issue to their rotations. Plus, they do not give any Frazzle DMG Amplify that Phoebe applies in ridiculous amounts, and they lack the Frazzle application for Zani to exploit her full combos. While the duo works together, Phoebe is a big upgrade, but worry not about clearing endgame content with Spectro Rover on the team — it's perfectly viable!

Spectro Rover is a great choice for Ciaccona in Spectro Frazzle teams, as they are able to apply Spectro Frazzle together quickly and efficiently, which allows them to match Confession Phoebe's level of application. Additionally, Ciaccona has the edge in multi-wave content as she is able to apply Spectro Frazzle off-field. This makes the duo hold a legitimate niche in Spectro Frazzle-based teams.

One of the usual Healing Support options that can slot into any team. Use her on Rejuvenating Glow with a Moonlit Clouds Spectro Rover. Super easy to use, provides amazing team-wide ATK% buffs and 15% DMG Amplify with one of the fastest rotations in the game. Enjoy.

Similar to Verina, a premium Healing Support option who can not only slot into any team, but also provide insane 12.5% Crit Rate, 25% Crit DMG, 25% ATK and 15% DMG Amplify buffs to your whole team. Use her on Rejuvenating Glow with a Moonlit Clouds Spectro Rover. One of the best but also easy to use characters in the game.
